messages:
incidents-bot: PAGED: Dedicated pool surge detected in eu-west-1. latency SLOs breached > 250ms for 10m, paging on-call.

alex: noticed spikes + error 429s for some tenants, autoscaler didn't add nodes. tagging @sam on-call.

sam: on it. any immediate customer-facing impact?

alex: ~12 customers with increased tail latency, 2 customers showing 429s on long-run requests.

jia: looking at autoscaler logs now. controller shows gating: safety_budget=0.0 and "burst_lock=true" for pool eu-west-1. scaling decisions suppressed.

maria: that safety budget lock was added yesterday to prevent runaway OOMs during canary; looks like the threshold is too strict for current steady surge.

sam: if safety_budget is 0.0 we can't scale. propose 1) temporarily relax safety_budget for eu-west-1, 2) enable burst_capacity toggle for the dedicated pool, 3) apply per-customer qps caps for top noisy tenants. opinions? :thinking_face:

jia: +1. I can flip burst_capacity=enabled and set safety_budget=0.25 via control plane CLI. patch will take ~30s to take effect.

ops-bot: NOTE: running cluster control command requires approver. Use /approve-scale if ready.

sam: i'm approving now. /approve-scale eu-west-1 emergency-burst

alex: also recommend temporarily disable prefetching (feature flag) for heavy customers, that reduces internal concurrent KV loads.

maria: drafting a short customer message for the 2 impacted tenants. will notify support to hold off on auto-escalation.

jia: running commands: 
```
control-plane set-pool eu-west-1 --burst-capacity enabled
control-plane set-pool eu-west-1 --safety-budget 0.25
control-plane scale-pool eu-west-1 --min-instances 12 --reason "emergency surge"
```

ops-bot: CHANGELOG: burst-capacity toggled, safety-budget updated, min-instances bumped. api response: accepted.

sam: monitoring. metrics show queue length and P99 dropping after ~45s. 429 rate down ~70%.

alex: applied per-tenant qps caps for tenant-a and tenant-b: cap=150 qps each. This will throttle noisy behaviors while we stabilize.

maria: sent customer note to tenant-a support alias: "We saw an elevated request pattern that impacted latency; we've temporarily enabled emergency capacity and applied short-term qps caps. We'll update when steady."

jia: logs: autoscaler decision now: reason=scale_up, added 4 instances, burst_enabled=true, gating cleared. sample log: 
```
autoscaler-controller: pool=eu-west-1 action=scale_up delta=4 new_target=14 reason=high_pending_ops
```

sam: great. leaving a summary for handoff. Lee, you're next on-call in 15m. current state: emergency burst enabled, safety_budget=0.25, min-instances 12, per-tenant qps caps on 2 tenants, prefetch disabled. Latency trending down but still above SLO for some requests. No data loss, no model regressions.

lee: ack. will monitor for next 1h, can revert safety_budget and burst when queue clears and p99 < 200ms for 30m. please leave notes for postmortem.

alex: note for postmortem: gating rule change rolled out yesterday reduced safety budget too aggressively; need rollback plan and a canary schedule.

maria: I'll open incident ticket and assign owners: root cause triage to infra + runtime teams, customer comms to support.

ops-bot: INCIDENT CREATED: #INC-2026-4829 assigned to infra/jia, runtime/alex, support/maria.

sam: closing loop here — mitigation applied and traffic shaping in place. will re-evaluate in 30m and update incident ticket. :white_check_mark:

lee: taking post-handoff watch. thanks team.
